meta.subtitle: Q2 segment momentum and contracted infrastructure growth against a rich trailing multiple and negative free cash flow

analystSentiment.commentary: We rate Select Water Solutions HOLD with a target range of $18.00 to $24.00 against a current price of $20.27. The second quarter was operationally strong: consolidated revenue of $395.8 million rose 8.7% year over year, and the Water Infrastructure and Chemical Technologies segments reached quarterly revenue of $101.6 million and $96.0 million. Net income was $22.6 million and Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure the company reports, was $92.7 million, each up sequentially. The stock has re-rated toward the top of its 52-week range of $9.29 to $22.55, and it now trades at rich trailing multiples of earnings and EV/EBITDA, which leaves little room for disappointment. Free cash flow was {- negative $79.9 million -} in FY25, and trailing net debt is 3.3x EBITDA. The infrastructure build-out is contracted and real, anchored by a 128-million-barrel minimum volume commitment signed in the quarter, but 2026 net capital expenditure guidance of $250 to $290 million keeps free cash flow under pressure near term. Seven analysts cover the name and all rate it a buy. We see the momentum as largely priced in and prefer to wait for free cash flow to turn before paying up.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Select Water Solutions, Inc. provides water management solutions to the energy industry in the United States. The company operates three segments: Water Infrastructure, Water Services, and Chemical Technologies. Water Infrastructure recycles, gathers, transfers, and disposes of produced water through pipelines, recycling and treatment facilities, storage, and saltwater disposal wells. Water Services covers water sourcing, transfer, flowback and well testing, containment, hauling, and monitoring, including the AquaView automation platform. Chemical Technologies supplies completion and production chemistry, including friction reducers and surfactants used in hydraulic fracturing and well completions. The company was formerly known as Select Energy Services, Inc. and changed its name to Select Water Solutions, Inc. in May 2023. It was founded in 2008 and is headquartered in Gainesville, Texas. FY25 revenue was $1.4 billion, down 3.1% year over year. The vendor reports the business as a single consolidated segment for the fiscal-year revenue mix, but management discloses these three operating lines in its quarterly reporting, and this report uses those segment figures where the filing provides them.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: Select Water Solutions is shifting toward contracted Water Infrastructure, which carries higher margins and steadier revenue than its legacy services work. The second quarter showed that shift working: Water Infrastructure revenue reached $101.6 million at a 58.3% gross margin before D&A, and the segment signed a 128-million-barrel minimum volume commitment over a seven-year term. The obstacle is price. At $20.27 the shares trade at steep trailing multiples of earnings and EBITDA, near the high end of their 52-week range. FY25 free cash flow was {- negative $79.9 million -}, and trailing net debt is 3.3x EBITDA. The infrastructure ramp is capital-heavy, with 2026 net capital expenditure guided to $250 to $290 million, so free cash flow is unlikely to turn sharply positive this year. We think the operational progress is real but largely discounted, which supports a HOLD rather than a chase.

catalysts: The Northern Delaware Basin pipeline tied to the new minimum volume commitment is expected to be operational within the next twelve months, adding firm contracted throughput.
Management guides third-quarter consolidated Adjusted EBITDA to $90 to $94 million, with Water Infrastructure revenue up 5% to 10% versus the second quarter.

Diversification agreements, including an ISE Chemicals iodine extraction facility and lithium partnerships expected to begin around 2027, could open new revenue streams from the existing water platform.

The strategic-alternatives review of the Peak Rentals business, begun in August 2025, could simplify the Water Services portfolio if a transaction emerges, though none was pending as of June 30, 2026.
risks: Valuation is the primary risk to the long side; the trailing earnings and EV/EBITDA multiples leave little room for a slowdown in completion activity.

The quarter's average WTI rose to $95.65 from $64.57 a quarter earlier on Middle East tensions, a supportive macro backdrop rather than the driver of activity, which the MD&A describes as stable and capital-disciplined; that oil-price support could reverse.
Negative free cash flow and a heavy 2026 capital program could push net leverage higher before it falls.
Demand is closely linked to oil and gas activity levels, and the company serves oil and gas producers concentrated in the Permian Basin.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: Second-quarter revenue was $395.8 million, up 8.7% year over year and up 8% sequentially. Net income was $22.6 million, compared with $9.4 million in Q1 2026 and $11.7 million in the second quarter of 2025. Total gross margin was 19.4%, up from 17.8% in the prior quarter and 15.9% a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, was $92.7 million, versus $77.6 million in Q1 2026 and $72.6 million a year earlier. By operating line, Water Infrastructure revenue was $101.6 million at a 58.3% gross margin before D&A, Chemical Technologies revenue was $96.0 million, and Water Services revenue was $198.2 million. The quarter caps a multi-year margin recovery: FY25 gross margin was 14.4% and operating margin 2.0%, up from a 2.7% gross margin in FY21. Revenue itself has declined for two years, {- down 8.4% -} in FY24 and {- down 3.1% -} in FY25, from a FY23 peak of $1.6 billion. FY25 diluted EPS was $0.21, down from $0.30 in FY24 and $0.72 in FY23. Consensus looks for FY26 EPS of $0.54 and FY27 EPS of $0.67.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: Total cash and cash equivalents were $33.4 million as of June 30, 2026, down from $56.0 million at March 31 and up from $18.1 million at December 31, 2025. The company had $250.0 million outstanding under the term loan of its sustainability-linked credit facility, $12.9 million under an agricultural loan tied to the Black River Ranch acquisition, and no borrowings on the revolver, compared with $70.0 million drawn on the revolver at December 31, 2025. The borrowing base was $264.0 million and total liquidity was $277.8 million, up from $163.6 million at year-end 2025. On a full-year FY25 basis, total debt was $316.3 million and net debt $298.2 million, trailing net debt is 3.3x EBITDA, and interest coverage is 2.1x. The current ratio was 1.58 on a trailing basis, down from 2.44 in FY21, and total equity was $0.9 billion at FY25. Management describes the balance sheet as healthy, but the leverage and coverage figures argue for caution while capital spending stays high.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Operating cash flow in the second quarter was $86.7 million, up from $10.2 million in Q1 2026 and $82.6 million a year earlier. Free cash flow, a non-GAAP measure, was $17.0 million in the quarter, after negative $67.1 million in Q1 2026 and $10.8 million in the second quarter of 2025. Net capital expenditure was $69.7 million, comprising $71.0 million of capital expenditure less $1.3 million of asset-sale proceeds, and the company also spent $42.0 million on acquisitions, including Black River Ranch. Management guides 2026 net capital expenditure to $250 to $290 million. FY25 free cash flow was {- negative $79.9 million -}, a {- negative 5.7% -} free-cash-flow margin, and the trailing FCF yield is {- negative 2.8% -}. FY25 capital expenditure was $294.6 million, above FY25 operating cash flow. The company still paid $33.7 million in dividends and repurchased $7.3 million of stock in FY25, and the dividend yield is 1.38%. Free cash flow needs to turn durably positive to support the current multiple, and the 2026 spending plan makes that unlikely this year.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: At $20.27 the shares trade at 72.4x trailing earnings, 45.7x trailing EV/EBITDA, and 2.0x trailing sales. On forward estimates the multiple compresses but stays full: the NTM P/E is 37.7x and the FY27 P/E is about 30.1x on consensus EPS of $0.67. These are high absolute multiples for an oilfield water-services business whose FY25 operating margin was 2.0% and whose revenue fell in each of the last two years. A peer set was captured, but it consists of regulated water utilities, which are not true comparables for an energy-levered services company with cyclical, activity-driven demand; we therefore do not anchor fair value to peer multiples and instead rely on the company's own economics and the scenarios below. The trailing multiples partly reflect depressed trailing earnings, with FY25 net income of only $21.2 million, so the ratios should ease as Adjusted EBITDA and net income recover. Even so, the current price already assumes a substantial earnings recovery, which limits upside if activity merely holds steady.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Water Infrastructure momentum continues, with revenue guided up 5% to 10% in the third quarter at 56% to 58% gross margins before D&A, and the 128-million-barrel minimum volume commitment plus newly conveyed disposal wells lift contracted throughput into 2027. Consensus FY27 EPS is met or exceeded and the shares hold a premium multiple, reaching the upper end of the Street's target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Second-quarter operating momentum holds, with consolidated revenue near $395.8 million and Adjusted EBITDA around the guided third-quarter range of $90 to $94 million, but the rich trailing multiple and negative free cash flow cap upside. The stock tracks the low end of the Street's target range and sits close to today's price.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Average WTI reverses from its elevated second-quarter level toward the prior quarter's average and completion activity slows. With FY25 free cash flow of negative $79.9 million and net debt at 3.3x EBITDA, the market de-rates the shares toward a mid-teens level as the growth premium unwinds.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: The scenarios weight to a fair value of $21.00, an expected upside of roughly 3.6% over the current price. The bear case sits 26% below the current price, so the reward-to-risk is skewed to the downside at about 0.14x, and that profile derives a HOLD. The base case assumes the operational momentum of the second quarter persists without a further re-rating, which we view as the central path given full trailing multiples. The bull case needs both the infrastructure ramp to deliver contracted volumes and the market to keep paying a premium multiple; the bear case needs the oil-price tailwind of the quarter to fade. We set the base probability at 45% and split the remainder 30% bull and 25% bear, reflecting a supportive Street, seven buys and a $24.00 consensus target, against a valuation that already discounts a strong recovery.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The vendor reports Select Water Solutions as a single consolidated segment, though management runs the business as three operating lines. Water Infrastructure recycles, gathers, transports, and disposes of produced water through pipelines, disposal wells, and storage; it generated $101.6 million in the second quarter at a 58.3% gross margin before D&A, up 26% from $80.9 million a year earlier. Water Services provides sourcing, transfer, flowback, hauling, and monitoring, and generated $198.2 million at a 23.0% gross margin before D&A. Chemical Technologies supplies friction reducers and surfactants for well completions, and generated $96.0 million at a 20.2% gross margin before D&A. Infrastructure earns a wider gross margin before D&A than the other two lines, and it is the segment management is prioritizing for capital and long-term contracts.

moatFactors.name: Contracted infrastructure and MVCs
moatFactors.body: Long-term contracts and minimum volume commitments create recurring, deficiency-protected revenue. In the second quarter the company signed a 128-million-barrel minimum volume commitment over a seven-year term and took ownership of 14 saltwater disposal wells as it extended its Northern Delaware Basin network. These arrangements raise switching costs for producers whose water is tied into the system.

moatFactors.name: Basin-scale physical network
moatFactors.body: The Northern Delaware Basin footprint includes about 1.7 million barrels per day of active fixed recycling capacity, more than 400 miles of pipeline, and 22.2 million barrels of storage across more than 1.5 million dedicated acres. A dense, interconnected network of pipelines and disposal wells is costly and slow for a competitor to replicate on the same acreage.

moatFactors.name: In-basin chemical manufacturing
moatFactors.body: In-basin manufacturing and continued product development let Chemical Technologies supply friction reducers and surfactants for complex completion designs, and management reports market-share gains in the segment. Chemicals are nonetheless more competitive and less asset-protected than the infrastructure business.

moatFactors.name: Cyclical, activity-driven demand
moatFactors.body: Demand is closely tied to oil and gas activity and produced-water volumes. Average WTI ran well above the prior quarter in the second quarter, and a reversal would pressure customer completion budgets, capping the durability of any advantage.

businessMoat.durability: The moat rests on physical infrastructure and contracts rather than on brand or technology, and it is strongest where the company owns dense pipeline and disposal networks tied to dedicated acreage. Minimum volume commitments and deficiency payments give some revenue visibility through a cycle, and the shift toward Water Infrastructure raises the share of higher-margin, contracted work. The limit is the underlying commodity cycle: revenue fell 8.4% in FY24 and 3.1% in FY25 as activity softened, and the business serves oil and gas producers whose budgets follow oil and gas prices. Diversification into iodine and lithium extraction and beneficial reuse could broaden the end markets, but those royalties are not expected until 2027 and are unproven at scale. On balance we see a narrow moat, widening in the infrastructure line but still capped by cyclicality.

points: Water Infrastructure revenue grew {+ 26% +} year over year to $101.6 million in the second quarter, and management guides a further 5% to 10% sequential increase in the third quarter.
The 128-million-barrel minimum volume commitment signed in the quarter, with a pipeline expected to be operational within twelve months, adds contracted throughput into 2027.
Chemical Technologies revenue rose {+ 23% +} sequentially to $96.0 million, aided by in-basin manufacturing and rising demand for surfactants.
Consensus expects revenue of about $1.5 billion in FY26, up roughly 9%, and $1.6 billion in FY27, with EPS rising from $0.54 to $0.67.
Diversification initiatives, an ISE Chemicals iodine facility and lithium royalty partnerships both targeted to begin in 2027, could add revenue from the existing water platform.

management.leadership: John D. Schmitz has served as President, Chief Executive Officer, and Chairman of the Board since January 2021. Christopher K. George is Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Michael C. Skarke is Executive Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, Michael J. Lyons is Executive Vice President and Chief Strategy & Technology Officer, and Cody J. Ortowski is Executive Vice President, Business and Regulatory Affairs. The combined chairman and chief executive roles are offset by a lead independent director, Richard A. Burnett, appointed in March 2023 and reaffirmed in February 2026. The proxy statement reports that 2023 performance share units tied to relative return on assets vested at 124% of target, while those tied to free cash flow vested at 90% of target over the period ending December 31, 2025.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital is flowing to Water Infrastructure, with 2026 net capital expenditure guided to $250 to $290 million. In the second quarter the company spent $69.7 million of net capital expenditure and $42.0 million on acquisitions, including Black River Ranch and disposal facilities in the Northern Delaware Basin. It also returned cash: FY25 dividends were $33.7 million and share repurchases $7.3 million, and the dividend yield is 1.38%. FY25 free cash flow was {- negative $79.9 million -}, so returns and growth spending were funded partly with the balance sheet rather than internally generated cash. The revolver carried $70.0 million at December 31, 2025 but was undrawn by June 30, 2026, though the $250.0 million term loan remained. The priority on contracted, higher-margin infrastructure is sensible, but it consumes cash while the payoff is still building.
management.governance: The proxy statement reports that all directors except Mr. Schmitz are independent under NYSE and NYSE Texas standards, namely Mmes. Burleson and Fielder and Messrs. Burnett, Cope, Fernandez-Moreno, Roberts, and Wall. The board combines the chairman and chief executive roles in Mr. Schmitz but names Mr. Burnett as lead independent director, who sets the agenda for and presides over executive sessions of the independent directors. Executive incentives are tied to Adjusted EBITDA, free cash flow, safety, environmental and sustainability performance, and other strategic goals, with 2025 annual bonuses funded at up to 94.1% of target. The company has a dual-class structure: Class B shares carry one vote each but no economic rights, and holders of SES Holdings units can exchange them for Class A shares or cash under the SES Holdings Agreement. That related-party exchange mechanism concentrates voting power and is a governance consideration for minority holders.
management.insiderOwnership: As of the March 10, 2026 record date, all current executive officers and directors as a group held 6.2% of Class A shares and 5.4% of combined voting power. John D. Schmitz beneficially owned 4,362,636 Class A shares, or 3.6%. Among outside holders, Crestview Partners II GP held 14.5% of combined voting power through Class A and Class B shares, and SES Legacy Holdings held all Class B shares, 11.7% of combined voting power. Franklin Mutual Advisors, BlackRock, Dimensional Fund Advisors at 5.2%, and The Vanguard Group at 5.0% each held more than 5% of Class A. The Class B structure ties voting power to the SES Holdings unitholders alongside the public Class A float.

idiosyncratic: Valuation is the main risk to the long side. The shares' rich trailing multiples price in a strong earnings recovery; if FY26 and FY27 EPS of $0.54 and $0.67 fall short, the multiple could compress sharply.

Free cash flow is negative and capital intensity is high. FY25 free cash flow was negative $79.9 million and 2026 net capital expenditure is guided to $250 to $290 million, so trailing leverage of 3.3x net debt to EBITDA, with interest coverage of 2.1x, could rise if EBITDA disappoints.

Demand is tied to a volatile commodity. The second quarter's average oil price ran well above the prior quarter's, and the MD&A notes that a potential release of previously sanctioned Venezuelan oil could depress prices and customer activity.

The dual-class structure concentrates control. Class B holders and SES Holdings unitholders, together with Crestview Partners at 14.5% of combined voting power, hold influence that public Class A holders do not, which can limit minority shareholders' say.
risks.systemic: Select Water Solutions is a levered play on North American upstream activity, which follows oil and natural gas prices. The MD&A describes a disciplined upstream environment early in 2026, with operators emphasizing capital efficiency and moderated production growth even as oil prices rose. Geopolitical shocks cut both ways: Middle East tensions lifted average WTI in the second quarter, but disruptions to shipping corridors and global chemicals markets could raise the company's input and logistics costs. A broad slowdown in drilling and completion activity, a sustained fall in oil prices, or higher-for-longer interest rates that raise the cost of capital would pressure both demand and the company's capital-intensive growth plan. These are market-level forces the company cannot control and that bear directly on a cyclical, activity-driven services model.

body: Our call is HOLD, with a fair-value target band of $18.00 to $24.00 around the $20.27 share price. The second quarter was genuinely strong, with net income of $22.6 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $92.7 million, and the strategic shift toward contracted, higher-margin infrastructure is working. But at the steep trailing multiples set out in the valuation section, near the top of the 52-week range, the market already reflects that progress.

The scenarios above imply only slim expected upside against a materially larger bear-case downside, so the reward/risk does not compensate for holding the shares at today's price. Negative FY25 free cash flow of $79.9 million and 2026 net capital expenditure of $250 to $290 million mean cash generation is unlikely to turn decisively positive this year. We would turn more constructive when free cash flow inflects positive or the shares de-rate toward the mid-to-high teens, closer to the bear-case level. Until then, the seven-buy Street consensus and its price target notwithstanding, HOLD is the disciplined call.
